transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's a burning, stinging feeling when I pass water, and I'm needing to go much more often than usual. It started about four days ago.
Can you tell me how much this is affecting your day-to-day life, and whether you have any allergies or have had bad reactions to medicines?

The stinging is about 5 out of 10 — uncomfortable, but I'm managing. I've stopped going to the residents' coffee morning though, in case I can't get to a toilet in time. As for medicines, I'm allergic to trimethoprim — it gave me an itchy rash.

Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have taken recently — including any new or changed ones and the dose if you know it — and also any long-term health problems, past illnesses, operations or hospital stays you've had?

I take levothyroxine 75 micrograms each morning, and alendronic acid 70 mg once a week for thin bones. I also use a vaginal cream from the hospital twice a week, but I'm afraid I can't remember its name. As for health problems, I have an underactive thyroid, and I had a water infection about a year ago that was treated with antibiotics — I haven't had any operations or hospital stays.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed that came along with this, or anything that’s been different since it started?
My urine looks cloudy and smells stronger than usual, though I haven't seen any blood in it. I've had no fever, shivers, back or side pain, or vomiting, and my niece hasn't noticed any new confusion.
Where do you feel the burning or stinging, and does it spread anywhere else?
It's when I pass water — a stinging feeling there. I haven't noticed it spreading anywhere else.

Other than the levothyroxine, alendronic acid and the vaginal cream you mentioned, is there anything else you take for your underactive thyroid, your thin bones, or that water infection from about a year ago, or is that all?
No, that's all — just the levothyroxine, the alendronic acid and the vaginal cream. The water infection a year ago was treated with antibiotics at the time, and I'm not on anything for it now.
Have you noticed anything that seems to make the stinging or needing to go more often better or worse—such as what you drink, what you’re doing, or anything else?
I can't say I've noticed anything making it better or worse — not what I drink or what I'm doing. It just seems to be there all the time.

Just to make sure I have the full picture, apart from your underactive thyroid, your thin bones, and that water infection a year ago, is there anything else you see a doctor or nurse about regularly, any other health condition your medicines are for, or any operations or hospital stays I should know about — or is that everything?
No, that's everything — just the thyroid, the thin bones and the water infection a year ago. I haven't had any operations or hospital stays.
What worries you most about this, and what are you hoping we can help with today?
I think it's another water infection, like the one I had a year ago, and I'm hoping to get antibiotics before the weekend. That's what worries me most — that it won't settle on its own.

Apart from what you’ve already told me, have you noticed anything else since this started—such as changes in appetite, sleep, weight or energy, or any changes in your bladder or bowel habits or breathing—or has nothing else changed?

Nothing else has changed with my appetite, weight, energy, breathing or my bowels. As for my bladder, I'm passing water about every hour in the day and getting up three or four times at night, when it's usually just once — but that's the needing to go I mentioned.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
